messages:
sara.support: FYI - ACME (tenant acme-prod) opened a P1. They see p95 ~400ms -> p99 spikes to 2s+ since ~03:20UTC and intermittent 502s. They attached traces showing GPU OOMs on gpool-7. Repro steps included a heavy batch run.

sara.support: Logs snippet from their side:
```
2026-03-17T03:21:05Z ERROR inference: runtime OOM tenant=acme-prod node=gpool-7 model=redwood-13b q8_0
2026-03-17T03:21:05Z WARN kv_cache: eviction_misses=23000 slab_frag=0.82
2026-03-17T03:21:06Z INFO request id=... latency=2150ms status=502
```

ben.runtime: assigning. Tagging @matt-sre and @alice-ml. Any recent deploys to gpool-7? @deploy-bot show last deploy

deploy-bot: last deploy to gpool-7 at 2026-03-17T02:58:12Z (runtime v2.14.0) - no hotfixes after that.

matt-sre: On it. Pulling node nvml + allocator stats now. Can you put tenant into throttled mode so we don't make it worse? curl to admin endpoint I can give.

tina-cs: Done — I set acme-prod throttled to 20 RPS at 03:34UTC and notified customer.

matt-sre: nvml shows GPU mem usage jumping then sudden drops when OOMs hit. Also seeing high host swap activity on node host-7.

alice-ml: KV cache growth looks abnormal for acme-prod (prefix-cache size growing without eviction). KV entries per-tenant: acme-prod=14.2M, typical=1.1M. Slab fragmentation high -> effective allocable memory reduced.

matt-sre: Good find. This screams KV growth + slab fragmentation -> allocator can't satisfy large contiguous allocs -> fall back path OOM + long GC/ejection leading to p99 tail.

sara.support: Customer mentioned they recently rolled a model change that increased average sequence length from 384 -> 1150 for some batches.

alice-ml: That also increases KV cache pressure (longer context -> bigger KV). Combine with batch/streaming pattern and you get sustained growth.

ben.runtime: Immediate mitigation plan:
- 1) Disable prefix/KV caching for acme-prod temporarily
- 2) Evict existing KV cache for that tenant
- 3) Restart the runtime process on gpool-7 nodes in a staggered rolling fashion (1 node at a time)
- 4) Apply allocator tuning flags on canary node and monitor

matt-sre: I'll run 1-2 now.

matt-sre: Command I used to disable cache for tenant (internal admin API):
```
curl -X POST -H "Authorization: Bearer $ADMIN" https://control-plane.internal/tenant/acme-prod/cache/disable
```

matt-sre: And to evict KV:
```
curl -X POST https://control-plane.internal/tenant/acme-prod/cache/evict -H "Authorization: Bearer $ADMIN"
```

ops-bot: eviction job queued on gpool-7 nodes (job id: evict-4419876543) — progress: 0/6

matt-sre: eviction completed on node host-7-3 and host-7-1. Memory pressure dropped ~30% on those.

ben.runtime: I'll schedule a rolling restart on remaining nodes at +5m intervals to avoid capacity dip.

alice-ml: Recommending allocator flag changes for testing on canary: set allocator.compact_slabs=true and allocator.max_slab_age=120s (force compaction) and lower kv_cache.max_entries_per_tenant=2e6 for acme-prod.

matt-sre: Applied flags on canary host-7-4 and restarted runtime. Early metrics show slab_frag drop from 0.82 -> 0.48 and p99 for that host down from 2.1s -> 360ms.

sara.support: Customer confirmed improved UX for throttled requests. They still want a permanent mitigation and a rollback safe plan.

ben.runtime: Next steps for a durable fix:
- Implement tenant-level KV caps & backpressure in runtime
- Add auto-evict heuristic when slab_frag > 0.7
- Harden allocator to allow compaction without full restart (longer-term)
- Document tenant guidance: avoid sudden seq-length/ batch multipliers or provide model variants

tina-cs: Customer prefers we keep cache disabled until we push per-tenant caps.

matt-sre: We'll keep acme-prod cache disabled and monitor for 48h. Also scheduling a deeper postmortem with metrics: per-tenant KV growth, slab fragmentation heatmap, p95/p99 curves, and timeline of customer model changes.

alice-ml: For release: will PR runtime change that exposes kv_cache.max_entries_per_tenant and slab compaction knobs, add default conservative caps, and include a warning in console when a tenant's kv usage exceeds 75% of slab band.

ben.runtime: Communicated to infra: allocate patch window Weds 03:00UTC to deploy canary changes, then gradual rollout across gpool pools.

sara.support: Marking incident resolved for customer for now (latency improved and 502s stopped). Keeping thread open for follow ups and postmortem notes.

tina-cs: Customer very appreciative of fast response :thumbsup:

matt-sre: I'll attach quick repro steps and traces to the incident ticket:
- reproduce with a synthetic job that sends 8 concurrent requests of seq_len 1024 with batch_size 8 and warm cache disabled
- observe KV growth and slab fragmentation over ~5-10 minutes

sara.support: Thanks team. I'll update ticket and schedule postmortem invite. """
